name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male Levite who served as a priest during the post-exilic period. He was the son of Hilkiah and father of Seriah, and is noted for explaining the law to the people, demonstrating his role in priestly teaching and leadership. As an Aaronic priest through Eleazar, he was also a signatory on the sealed covenant document, emphasizing his recognized authority and commitment to the covenant community.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that highlights divine assistance. This proper name underscores the believer's dependence on God's help and presence in their service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Azariah was the son of Hilkiah and the father of Seriah, situating him within a priestly lineage. These relationships affirm his place in the Levitical priesthood and continuity of priestly service.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his priestly role during a critical time of restoration for Israel. By explaining the law to the people, he contributed to the spiritual renewal and understanding of God's covenant. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document further marks him as a key leader committed to upholding God's law and the community's faithfulness. His lineage and priestly service exemplify the importance of faithful transmission of God's word and covenant obedience in the post-exilic period.
